distribution.rationale: Reference type determines whether a stablecoin is an EMT (single currency) or ART (basket/other), which feeds the legal category; the corpus ties stablecoin classes to the regulatory category.

citations.quote: ‘electronic money token’ or ‘e-money token’ means a type of crypto-asset that purports to maintain a stable value by referencing the value of one official currency

distribution.rationale: The reference asset is the defining criterion separating EMT, ART and payment stablecoin classes, so X refines the stablecoin class question along the referenced-asset axis.

citations.quote: ‘asset-referenced token’ means a type of crypto-asset that is not an electronic money token and that purports to maintain a stable value by referencing another value or right or a combination thereof

distribution.rationale: Both concern the currency to which a stablecoin pegs; the candidate asks whether the peg is a fiat currency, which is a specific case of X's single-official-currency value.

citations.quote: “qualifying stablecoin” has the meaning given by article 88G of the Regulated Activities Order

distribution.rationale: Redemption is tied to the reference asset, but redemption mechanism asks how conversion happens rather than what asset is referenced, so only partial specialisation.

citations.quote: The cryptoasset is designed to be redeemable for a predefined amount of a reference asset or assets (eg 1 USD, 1 oz gold)

distribution.rationale: Stablecoin reference shapes payment or investment use, but function is a broader purpose dimension that does not classify the referenced asset.
Reference type is a top-level stablecoin dimension with no clearly more general asset dimension covering it fully.
Issuer identifiability is a structural precondition for classifying assets under issuer-based regimes (MiCA issuer obligations), so it informs but does not itself define the legal category.

citations.quote: This Regulation does not apply to crypto-assets that are unique and not fungible with other crypto-assets.

distribution.rationale: Identifiable issuer status and centralisation of control over minting and governance overlap heavily; the corpus ties no identifiable issuer to decentralised assets.

citations.section: Sections 1-5: motivation, related work, methodology, taxonomy dimensions, dataclass and decision rules, mapping results (summary)
citations.quote: Where crypto-assets have no identifiable issuer, they should not fall within the scope of Title II, III or IV

distribution.rationale: Issuer identifiability is a distinct, top-level question about who creates the asset, not a specialisation of any listed dimension.
Issuer presence determines who can perform off-chain redemption, but redemption is a separate question about the holder's conversion route.
Issuer presence does not determine the economic purpose of the asset, though issuer type can correlate with function.
Scope criteria define what counts as a crypto-asset; issuer identifiability is a separate attribute that applies after the asset is in scope.
